about: Audio for the Arabic course: one synthesised voice, made from the exact vowelled text and listened to before it ships. Each clip belongs to its exact text, so one clip serves every place that text appears. Which texts have a voice is defined in app/scripts/arabic-voice-sources.mjs (specs/arabic-audio-course.md). MyDay’s own add-on: the curriculum package’s audio_status describes the course’s own materials and is unchanged. Made by app/scripts/make-arabic-audio.mjs; checked at every build by app/scripts/prepare-audio.mjs.

voice.name: ar-XA-Chirp3-HD-Charon
voice.kind: Chirp 3 HD prebuilt voice (not a custom or cloned voice)
voice.settings: MP3, 24 kHz, normal speed; slower playback is done by the browser

label: Synthesised voice — a model to copy; checked by ear, not yet by a teacher.
terms: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, prebuilt voice, generally available for Arabic (checked 19 October 2026): no attribution required; generated content isn’t presented as a human recording (the app labels it “Synthesised voice”).

checks.to check: made, not yet listened to: not shipped
checks.checked: listened to against the text: shipped
checks.redo: heard a mistake: made again next run
checks.left out: couldn’t be made right: no play button

rounds.listening: All 96 clips listened to against the vowelled text and its reading, by ear, by MyDay’s learner (basic Arabic), on 19 October 2026 — not yet by an Arabic teacher. Before that, the voice was chosen in a blind trial (10 clips, 4 voices).
rounds.cross_check: Every clip was also transcribed, fully vowelled, by a second model (Gemini 3.8 Flash) and compared with its text; clips it heard differently were made again until it agreed (three clips, four retakes; each marked “earlier”). A transcription can mishear too: this flags clips to listen to, it doesn’t approve them.

removed.reason: Their sentences were corrected in curriculum 1.1.2 and its teaching companion (review of 23 October 2026); a clip belongs to its exact text, so the old voice cannot stay. The corrected sentences have no play button until new clips are made and listened to.
A course-word note put two Arabic pieces side by side (مَا رَأْيُكِ؟ and رَأْي), so they were voiced as one clip; the note now separates them and each has its own clip.
